skill.name: designing-tests
skill.description: Guides test strategy, framework choice, test templates, coverage targets, mocking, and validation loops for software projects.
skill.summary: Helps teams design practical unit, integration, and end-to-end tests with clear coverage goals.
skill.author: CloudAI-X

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, mock HTTP examples, and ordinary test templates. The skill does instruct agents to run npm test commands, which can execute project-defined scripts and should require user approval in untrusted repositories. No prompt injection or data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Test command execution can run project-defined scripts.
remediation.suggestion: Tell agents to inspect package scripts and ask for user approval before running npm test commands in untrusted repositories.

remediation.issue: Validation guidance lacks sandbox and trust-boundary notes.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to run tests only in trusted workspaces or isolated environments when repository provenance is unclear.

content.value_statement: Many teams add tests without a clear plan, which creates gaps and slow suites. This skill guides test type selection, templates, coverage targets, and validation steps.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use unit, integration, component, API, and end-to-end tests.
Recommends testing frameworks for JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, and Go projects.
Provides reusable structures for unit, integration, and end-to-end test cases.
Defines coverage targets for business logic, edge cases, API contracts, and user paths.
Guides test data factories, fixtures, mocking, and deterministic time handling.
Describes a validation loop for running tests, checking coverage, and fixing failures.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not a complete test suite for every project.
Framework recommendations may need adjustment for existing project standards.
Test commands should be reviewed before running in untrusted repositories.
Coverage targets are general defaults and may not match regulated environments.

use_cases.title: Plan coverage for a new feature
use_cases.description: Map expected behavior, edge cases, and user journeys to the right test levels before implementation.

use_cases.title: Standardize team testing practices
use_cases.description: Choose framework patterns, coverage expectations, and mocking rules for a shared engineering workflow.

use_cases.title: Improve weak or flaky suites
use_cases.description: Review failing tests, isolate unstable dependencies, and add missing cases around critical behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Choose test types
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a small change
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the designing-tests skill to identify which unit, integration, and end-to-end tests I need for this feature.

prompt_templates.title: Draft test cases
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the designing-tests skill to propose test cases for this module, including edge cases, fixtures, and expected assertions.

prompt_templates.title: Improve coverage strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the designing-tests skill to review this test suite and recommend coverage improvements by risk, speed, and reliability.

prompt_templates.title: Design full test infrastructure
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the designing-tests skill to design a testing strategy for this repository, including frameworks, data setup, mocks, coverage targets, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: I need tests for a user registration API.
output: Recommended split: unit tests for validation rules, integration tests for API behavior, and one end-to-end registration path.
Key cases: valid registration, duplicate email, weak password, malformed email, persistence failure, and response contract checks.
Data setup should use a user factory and reset state between tests.

output_examples.input: Our tests pass locally but coverage is low.
output: Focus first on business logic, error handling, and API contracts before UI snapshots.
Review uncovered branches and add cases for failure paths, boundary values, and authorization rules.
Keep slow end-to-end tests limited to critical user journeys.

output_examples.input: We need a testing standard for a TypeScript service.
output: Use a fast unit test runner for isolated logic and a request-level integration layer for service contracts.
Mock external services at boundaries and avoid mocking internal modules by default.
Set coverage thresholds, require clear test names, and run the suite multiple times for flaky areas.

best_practices: Start with behavior and risk, then choose the smallest reliable test type.
Use factories, fixtures, and mocks to keep tests deterministic and independent.
Validate new tests by running the suite, checking coverage, and addressing flaky failures.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on snapshot tests as the main proof of important behavior.
Do not mock the code under test or hide broken internal logic.
Do not run project scripts in untrusted repositories without reviewing their behavior first.

faq.question: What test types does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers unit, integration, API, component, and end-to-end testing patterns.

faq.question: Can it choose a testing framework?
faq.answer: Yes. It suggests common frameworks for JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, and Go projects.

faq.question: Does it write complete tests automatically?
faq.answer: It provides structures and guidance. Final tests still need project-specific implementation details.

faq.question: How does it handle coverage?
faq.answer: It recommends target areas and threshold examples for business logic, APIs, and critical user paths.

faq.question: Is it useful for existing test suites?
faq.answer: Yes. It can help identify gaps, improve flaky tests, and strengthen validation workflows.

faq.question: Should agents run the listed test commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. Test commands should be reviewed and approved, especially in untrusted repositories.
